subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the domain of the real valued function f(x) = 1/√(|x| − x).

mark_split.label: Condition for the function to be defined

recall_prompt: Say how you would find this domain — the conditions the formula forces, and the answer.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Test both cases of the modulus
steps.margin_note: One of the two marks is for the condition alone. Write the strict inequality first, then split the modulus at 0.
steps.memory_tip: The root sits in a denominator, so ≥ 0 becomes > 0, and that single change removes every x ≥ 0.
lines: The root is in a denominator, so it must be
If x ≥ 0 then |x| = x, so |x| − x = 0, which fails

recall.must_convey: That the root is in a denominator, so |x| − x must be strictly positive, and that this fails for every x ≥ 0 because the value there is 0.
accept: strictly greater than zero because the root is in the denominator
for x at least zero the inside is zero so the denominator is zero and it fails
only negative x gives minus two x which is positive
denominator lo undi so zero avvakoodadu strictly positive undali
the condition is strict so the right half of the line goes out

steps.why: √(|x| − x) is 0 for every x ≥ 0. A zero is allowed under a root but not under a root in a denominator, so the whole right half of the line is lost here.
common_mistakes: Using ≥ 0 and answering R, which is the answer to the same expression without the fraction.
Including x = 0, where the denominator is √0 = 0.

steps.label: Write the domain
steps.margin_note: The second mark is the interval itself. Write it in interval form, and check every bracket.
steps.memory_tip: Open at 0: the point where the two cases meet is exactly where the denominator is zero.
lines: Only x < 0 makes |x| − x strictly positive.

recall.must_convey: That the domain is every negative real number, written as the open interval minus infinity to 0.
accept: minus infinity to zero open at zero
zero kanna takkuva unna anni numbers
the negative half line with zero excluded

steps.why: Only x < 0 makes |x| − x strictly positive, so the domain is the negative half of the line with 0 itself excluded.
common_mistakes: Writing (−∞, 0] and including 0, where the function is undefined.
Writing (0, ∞), the wrong half of the line.
